_comment: Ships trade: they buy a commodity at one port and sell it at the next (see data/markets.json, where ships also buy their own fuel at a price that follows the local oil price). starting_money covers a first ship and its first cargo. Breakdowns: every interval_s seconds, each ship at sea (not recovery boats) rolls its own chance of losing hit of its maintenance (0.5 = 50 points). The chance runs from chance_at_full at 100% maintenance to chance_at_empty at 0%, times the model's breakdown_factor (bigger ships are sturdier), times an age factor (1 + age_per_hour_at_sea for each hour the ship has spent at sea, up to max_age_factor), less the durability skill. initial_view_width_deg: how many degrees of the globe the map shows across when it opens, centered on the home port.
_company_colors_comment: Colors a new company can choose (its name in the top bar and the rings around its HQ and hubs): [id, name, hex], in picker order.
_seasons_comment: Seasonal closures (scripts/sim/seasons.gd), for saves founded with them. Each closure shuts a canal's locks (canal), some ports (ports) or a stretch of sea (circles: [lon, lat, radius nm]; every lane through it) from from to to ([month, day], wrapping past the new year when from is later), on its real dates; not_first_year spares the game's first calendar year; ice is the circles of frozen water drawn on the map (else its circles or its icebreaker area's). A ship won't start a leg it can't finish before one shuts: it waits in port (not a hold: nothing for the player to do) until it reopens; ships already at sea finish. label names a stretch of sea on the map all year (at the middle of its circles). ice ([lon, lat, radius nm] circles) is where a port closure's sea ice is drawn on the map (closures over a stretch of sea, and those an icebreaker area covers, draw their own circles). Ice zones stay open, but ships within radius_nm of center (lon, lat) crawl at speed and wear faster (wear) in their season, fuel per mile the same. The activity log warns warn_days calendar days before a closure that touches the player's ports or routes, and when it shuts and reopens.
_icebreaking_comment: Icebreakers (scripts/sim/icebreaking.gd). Each ice area is covered by circles ([lon, lat, radius nm]) and is in season while its seasonal closure (closure) or ice zone (zone) is. With an icebreaker stationed there (station_ports: where it waits), the closure is lifted for ships it can lead (the Great Lakes locks still shut regardless): ships reaching the ice edge, or leaving a port in the ice, wait (engines off) for the icebreaker, which leads up to convoy_size ships on the same lane through the ice at escort_speed (by icebreaker kind: a share of the slower of it and the slowest ship), gap_nm apart (wide enough that each ship shows on its own at the opening zoom), then goes back for the next. An ice zone that stays open anyway (the Gulf of Finland) has no convoys: an icebreaker stationed there keeps the fairways open, so ships in it sail at fairway speed and wear instead of crawling. Icebreakers pay their own fuel and repairs.
_docks_comment: Berths (scripts/sim/docks.gd; the marina each port is drawn as, scripts/ui/map_view.gd): each port size band's berths in order round its marina (the +y side from the entrance in, then the -y side: the first each side along the first pier's seaward face, open to the outer harbour, then one between each pier and the next, the last along the land end), one letter each: L a long pier that takes any ship the port takes (the rule now: every pier is as long as the longest ship the port takes), s a berth only for the smaller ships (those that can dock at a Small port), m one for any ship a Medium port takes, B an old big berth only the biggest ships use. hub_berths: any port with an HQ or hub, so any HQ or hub can take the biggest ships. Cargo ships queue at the anchorage for a berth, first come first served, come in through the entrance and down the channel, round into their slot and alongside, and pull out backwards, at their own speed (slowing only to come alongside, sliding the last slide_s on their thrusters; in_s and out_s when there's no map to measure the way); a ship with nothing to do comes in to a pier while the port has berths to spare, else lies at the anchorage; tugs moor along the inside of the jetty's arms, other service ships lie at the anchorage.
_weather_comment: Storms (scripts/sim/weather.gd), for saves founded with Moderate or Harsh storms. They slow ships, wear them and make breakdowns likelier, and the strongest hurricane, typhoon and cyclone cores close ports; in saves without storms nothing happens to ships, though storms are still drawn. levels: slow is the most a storm's core cuts speed (fuel per mile stays the same, so a storm alone can't strand a ship), wear the most it multiplies wear and breakdown chance, close_at how strong a tropical storm must be over a port to close it (0..1), rate how many storms form, times the basins' per_year. Each basin forms storms of its kind in its months (1-12; peak months twice as often), per_year a year on average, somewhere in spawn ([[lon min, lon max], [lat min, lat max]]), with a radius_nm of effect, lasting life_days (a calendar day is 72 s of play), moving speed_nm calendar nm an hour (about knots). Tropical kinds (hurricane, typhoon, cyclone) drift west and poleward, then curve away east past recurve_lat; gales run east. names are used in turn.
_calendar_comment: The in-game calendar starts at start (UTC) and runs minutes_per_second calendar minutes per second of play at 1x: since 2026-10-22 (the living world) 80, so a game year is about 1.8 hours of play; ships keep their on-screen speeds, so in calendar terms they sail at a quarter of their real speed (Shanghai to Rotterdam about 4 months). pace is how much faster that is than the old calendar (20 a second, matched to real knots): the things a player waits for in real time (fishing trips, research station time and deadlines, cruise dwell and refits, rig waits, the Divine powers' cooldowns, closure warnings, storm movement) are stretched by it in calendar days so they take the same play time as before, and money and output per calendar time (wages, upkeep, interest, plants' output, cruise fares) were divided by it so earnings an hour of play stayed as they were. The world's own facts (seasons, harvests, people, the economy's days of cover) run on the calendar as it is.
_rough_seas_comment: Rough seas far south: ships wear wear_factor times as fast south of lat, and cargo on legs to or from a port south of it sells for pay_bonus more. upper_lakes_bonus: cargo on legs between two ports on the upper Great Lakes (Superior, Michigan, Huron: ports.json lake) sells for that much more, like the real ore and grain trade.
_currents_comment: Ocean currents (data/currents.json, Currents). A ship sails faster with a current and slower against it, by (ref_speed_kn + the current along its way) / ref_speed_kn, at most limit either way (fuel burns by the second, so it follows the time). The lane tool (--currents-only) plans a second way round for a lane, one way, riding a current, where it beats the lane by at least min_gain of the time in some months and is at most max_detour times as long; a ship takes it in those months. ride_min_nm: the least a second way rides a current; cut_nm: how far from each port it leaves and rejoins the lane (beyond the approach channels).
_harbor_speed_comment: Ships easing out of port and into the next at sea: leaving, a ship would build up from start x its speed to full speed over about seconds of sailing (steady acceleration), and arriving slow the same way, in steps pieces each (the zones fuel, range and arrival times are worked out over, like the convoy canals); on a leg too short for both, each takes half of it. start 1.0: off, ships keep their speed right up to the harbour mouth and away from it (they get going and slow down inside their marina instead: scripts/ui/map_view.gd _sailed_share()).
_port_fee_comment: A share of each trade's margin (what the cargo sold for, less what it cost; nothing on a loss) paid as a port fee where a cargo is sold, at every port the company has no HQ or hub at.
_crew_comment: Crew wages (scripts/autoload/game_state.gd _pay_wages()): every ship has captains and crew by its tier (ship_models.json tier 1-5: captains[tier - 1] and crew[tier - 1]), paid every period_days calendar days (eight weeks, about 17 minutes of play): captain_wage a captain and crew_wage a crew member, for every ship that worked in that time (sailing, or doing a stop in port); ships idle the whole time pay nothing. Set so wages are about 20% of a Scooter's profit and 5% of a Dominator's on an average route. They may take the company's money below $0: a company in debt runs its ships on credit but can't buy anything until it's back above $0.
_loans_comment: Loans (scripts/autoload/game_state.gd take_loan()): on the Finances screen a company can borrow step at a time up to max, and pay it back a step at a time; yearly_interest is charged on what it owes, a period's share each crew payday.
_tugs_comment: Tugs (ship_models.json tug): you can own per_port of them for each port on your ships' routes, each based at the route port with the fewest (the busiest first). A ship lost within a tug's reach (reach_nm, more with the range skill) of either end of its leg is fetched by the free tugs based at the nearer end that can reach it (up to per_port), before any recovery boat: they sail out, turn round and push or drag it back to their port at tow_factor x each one's speed, added up (so two tow it twice as fast as one). Each earns recovery_xp per_nm for every mile of the job.
_port_sizes_comment: Port sizes run 1 to max: bands are [name, smallest size] (Small 1-25, Medium 26-50, Large 51-75, Giant 76-100); ports.json size is where each starts. A port grows by the cargo value the player's ships load and unload there: value / (growth_value_per_point x its size) points (bigger ports need more), banked up to max_pending and applied at up to max_growth_per_hour. Tuned so a mid-game company's busiest port (about $60M an hour through a size-50 port) climbs a band in about 15 hours, and no port faster than a band in 5 hours. (Shrinking comes back with the new economy.) Sizes in the normal range play as before sizes; toward size 1 the player's trades move prices up to impact_at_min times as much (and their effect lasts that much longer) and fuel and repairs cost costs_at_min more, and toward max impact_at_max and costs_at_max. ship_models.json min_port is the smallest band a model can dock at.
_hubs_comment: Headquarters and hubs: the HQ is at the home port from the start; a company may found any number of hubs, each placed for good at any port: the first after the HQ costs price, each next price_growth times the last (M, M, M...), and each hub (not the HQ) pays upkeep_month by its port's size band every calendar month. Hub facilities come later (DESIGN_LIVING_WORLD.md). industry: each hub (and the HQ) has INDUSTRY_SLOTS plots for its warehouses beside its marina (a warehouse, stockyard, cold store or terminal for one commodity: GameState.industry_name()), all open; each is one commodity's (and every good of its kind: a maker's cars count as Cars), one of each per hub, costs price, and demolishing it refunds refund of that. For its commodity at its port it makes the buy price buy_discount cheaper and the sell price sell_bonus more expensive, the HQ's hq_multiplier times as much. The Cargo & Ore type's own mines, plants and factories are data/industry.json's (Industry).
_company_types_comment: Company types (a company's divisions): a new company starts as one type (chosen on the New Company screen) and can buy into any other at any time for division_price (GameState.choose_company_type()). A company may buy every model of its types; ship categories not in any type (recovery boats, tugs, icebreakers) are for every company (Progression.can_buy_model()). categories: the ship_models.json categories each type sells; tab: its Shop tab; color: its icon's color (CompanyTypeIcon draws the icon by id). pick_only: a type that can't be a company's first, only bought as a division (Research). coming_soon: a type not playable yet: it can't be chosen, and its models (ship_models.json coming_soon) are only shown in the Shop's coming-soon tab.

types.name: Cargo & Ore
types.blurb: Mines, smelters and factories of your own, and the ships between them: ore carriers with thirteen ores, breakbulk carriers with steel, metals and timber, and container ships with thirteen kinds of goods.

types.name: Vehicles
types.blurb: Car carriers and boat carriers shipping for 44 carmakers and boatbuilders, budget to luxury: win their trust and build factories of your own for them.

types.name: Agriculture
types.blurb: Farms at the world's farm ports, and the ships to carry their harvest: grain carriers with grain, coffee, cocoa, sugar and spices, Fresh produce carriers with fruit, berries and vegetables, and livestock carriers with cattle, sheep, pigs and horses.

types.name: Tankers
types.blurb: Oil and gas: tankers with crude, diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, gas carriers with LNG, LPG, ammonia and hydrogen, and your own oil rigs, gas platforms and refineries (see the Energy tab).

types.name: Seafood
types.blurb: Fishing and crabbing boats working the grounds for salmon, tuna and king crab, and reefers carrying the catch to market.

types.name: Cruises
types.blurb: Cruise lines: Ocean cruisers filling big ships at big ports, and Expedition cruisers taking a few guests to the ice, the wildlife and the wonders. You set the itineraries, the cabins, the prices and the service.

types.name: Research
types.blurb: Survey vessels and deep-sea motherships exploring over 200 real places under the sea: the trenches, the Titanic, vents, sunken cities and more. Contracts pay; your own expeditions earn research points, a journal and big perks for the whole company. Taken at a pick, never as a start.

_cruises_comment: Cruise lines (scripts/sim/cruises.gd, Cruises). A cruise ship sails round trips: its route's first port is its home port (the HQ, a hub, or a port with the company's cruise terminal: terminal_costs, the first then each after), the rest its ports of call. In its home port it takes bookings till its departure rule says go (departures: after days, at fill, or both: once at fill it books on till the days are up or it's full, sailing at the days anyway); tickets are paid as it sails, then each port of call charges port_fee_per_guest and pays excursion commission, and back home its guests' onboard spending is paid and its supplies, amenity upkeep and entertainment are charged, and the voyage gets a review. Cabins: space shares in share_step % steps; each class's guests take units of space (Interior 1, Ocean View 1.25, Balcony 1.6, Suite 3); a model's guests are for balanced_mix. Recommended price per guest = night_price (Ocean; Expedition x expedition_price_factor) x nights x rating x route x season x package x ship factors (each shown). Bookings: a home port's would-be cruisers a game day are pool_per_size x its size x its season, shared by every cruise ship booking there by its berths; a ship books toward its ceiling, the share of its berths that will pay its price: price_curve [price / recommended, share] (0.9 at the recommended price). Onboard spending and excursions are per guest-night and per guest at each port of call (excursion_per_attraction more per attraction near the port); a package includes them in the ticket (and the recommended price). Service levels (Basic to Luxury) set supplies per guest-night (food), crew (the Crew dial times the model's crew, so wages) and entertainment per guest-night, and add to guest experience. Amenities fill deck slots: cost (x the model's price), upkeep per guest-night, onboard spending bonus, experience points, and which line can fit them. Refits (cabins, amenities, looks; at the HQ or a hub): refit_days plus refit_days_per_change, costing refit_cost (x the model's price) for cabins and looks changes besides the amenities' own. Breakdowns refund breakdown_refund of the tickets, a loss loss_refund (rescue_refund instead if it's rescued). Seasons: per area (by home port latitude and longitude), 12 monthly demand factors.
_facilities_comment: Hub facilities (Hub.facilities, GameState.build_facility(); DESIGN_LIVING_WORLD.md M1): one of each may be built at a hub for price, paying upkeep_month, each with one effect at that port for the company's ships (the HQ's hq_multiplier times a hub's): dock (that much shorter stops for the categories), fuel (cheaper fuel), repairs (cheaper repairs), price (dearer sales of the family's goods), passengers (a bigger pool of cruise guests booking there), cold (the farm store there is a cold store).

facilities.name: Container terminal
facilities.text: Gantry cranes along the quay: container ships load and unload a third faster here.

facilities.name: Bulk conveyor
facilities.text: Conveyors and grabs for the bulk carriers: ore, grain and breakbulk ships turn round a third faster.

facilities.name: Tank farm
facilities.text: Tanks and manifolds on the quay: tankers and gas carriers pump out a third faster.

facilities.name: Ro-ro ramp
facilities.text: A ramp and a marshalling yard: car and boat carriers drive off a third faster.

facilities.name: Cold store
facilities.text: Refrigerated sheds: your farm store here keeps its produce fresh for longer, and the catch landed here keeps.

facilities.name: Fish market
facilities.text: An auction hall by the quay: your catch and seafood cargo sell for more here.

facilities.name: Cruise terminal
facilities.text: A proper terminal with check-in halls: a third more guests book cruises from here.

facilities.name: Bunkering station
facilities.text: Your own bunker barges and tanks: fuel costs a tenth less here.

facilities.name: Drydock
facilities.text: A graving dock and workshops: repairs cost a quarter less here (and the refits of the future are done here).
